extra.message: The code makes HTTPS requests with SSL certificate verification disabled (ssl._create_unverified_context()). This exposes the application to man-in-the-middle attacks where an attacker can intercept or modify traffic to the partner endpoint.

The endpoint reflects the Origin header directly into Access-Control-Allow-Origin without validation, and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials to true. This allows any website to make authenticated cross-origin requests, potentially exposing sensitive data to malicious sites.

The endpoint disables XSS protection (X-XSS-Protection: 0) and clears the Content-Security-Policy header. These security headers are designed to protect against XSS attacks, and their removal makes the application more vulnerable to injection attacks.

A hardcoded default SECRET_KEY is present in the source code. If the environment variable is not set in production, this predictable key will be used for JWT signing, allowing attackers to forge authentication tokens and impersonate any user.

The code uses Python's random module (Mersenne Twister) for generating security-sensitive codes. This PRNG is not cryptographically secure and can be predicted if enough output is observed. Should use secrets module or SystemRandom for security tokens.
